material_definitions: Lithium-stuffed garnet-type oxide solid electrolytes (LLBZT) were developed by simultaneous substitution of Ta5+ into the Zr4+ site and Ba2+ into the La3+ site in Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZ).
The overall formula is Li6.5La3−xBaxZr1.5−xTa0.5+xO12, where Ba contents x range from 0 to 0.3.
All LLBZT samples possess a cubic garnet structure without secondary phases.
The relative densities of LLBZT are between 89 and 93%.
Lithium-stuffed garnet-type oxide solid electrolytes (LLBZT) were developed by simultaneous substitution of Ta5+ into the Zr4+ site and Ba2+ into the La3+ site in Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZ).
The overall formula is Li6.5La3−xBaxZr1.5−xTa0.5+xO12, where Ba contents x range from 0 to 0.3.
All LLBZT samples possess a cubic garnet structure without secondary phases.
The relative densities of LLBZT are between 89 and 93%.
LLBZT oxides with fixed Li content of 6.5 but different Ba content x = 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.20, and 0.30 were prepared by a conventional solid state reaction method.
Stoichiometric amounts of LiOH 7H2O (10% excess), La(OH)3, BaCO3, ZrO2, and Ta2O5 were used in the synthesis.
The synthesis involved calcination at 900 0C for 6 h, pressing into pellets, and final sintering at 1150 0C for 15 h in air using a Pt 1Au 5% alloy crucible.
The conductivity of each LLBZT sample was evaluated with AC impedance measurements at a temperature from 27 to 100 0C.

material_definitions: Garnet-type LLBZT solid solutions were synthesized with varying Ba contents (x=0 to 0.3).
Samples were prepared via solid state synthesis, sintered at 1150°C.
Conductivity was measured using AC impedance spectroscopy with Li-ion-blocking Au electrodes.
Total conductivity includes contributions from both bulk and grain boundaries.
